newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia watchdog warns share manipulators.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia watchdog warns share manipulators.

text.p: The head of Indonesia's Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam) on Friday warned against attempts to manipulate stock prices.

"Don't try to manipulate prices. We are watching closely. We will intervene in the market if necessary," I Gede Putu Ary Suta told reporters while attending a two-day conference on capital flows on the island of Bali.
Suta was responding to questions on recent heavy fluctuations in stock prices, especially in second- and third-line stocks on the Jakarta Stock Exchange (JSE).
"It's the duty of the JSE to act if prices are fluctuating. We will only intervene if the JSE is not doing its job," he said.
Suta said the recent swings in the price of Astra International shares had not violated capital market laws.

Astra, the country's largest automobile manufacturer, gained sharply last week on reported comments by timber tycoon Muhamad (Bob) Hasan that the Nusamba group he controls was interested in buying into the company.
